question.text: During a merger of Company A (transferor) into Company B (transferee), Anand holds 1,000 demat shares of Company A. The approved exchange ratio is 3:5 (3 shares of B for every 5 shares of A). According to the scheme, what does Anand receive?

answer.text: He retains his 1,000 shares of Company A unchanged
He receives 1,667 shares of Company B in addition to retaining his Company A shares
He must sell his Company A shares on the stock exchange before the merger completes
Anand receives 600 shares of Company B according to the scheme

explanation.text: The Logic: A scheme of merger/amalgamation defines the number of shares exchanged or issued, and the R&T agent calculates entitlement as per the scheme. At 3:5 (3 shares of B for every 5 shares of A), Anand's 1,000 shares of A translate to (3/5) x 1,000 = 600 shares of Company B. The Trap: Candidates may reverse the ratio (getting 1,667 shares) or think existing shares are retained alongside the new shares. The entitlement follows the exchange ratio set out in the scheme. Note: The R&T agent's role is to apply the scheme's defined exchange ratio to each holder's pre-merger balance.
